bandReport.notes: Pages map to printed booklet pages 29, 31, 33, 35 (booklet LVPK-O-PSO/56A). Items 61-80, no gaps and no repeats. Item 61 opens at the top of p14-c1 and item 80 closes at the foot of p17-c2 above '[ P.T.O.', so both band edges are clean and nothing spills past them. Two items span the gutter and were assembled c1-then-c2 as the brief requires: Q63 (Statement I/II in p14-c1; its 'Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?' lead-in plus all four options at the top of p14-c2) and Q68 (stem plus statement I in p15-c1; statements II/III plus options in p15-c2). Every other item is whole within a single column. Column crops all looked cleanly split; no sliced lines and no item number missing from the top of any c2. p16-c2 carries two tiny stray ink marks at its extreme left edge (around the vertical middle) which are page-edge/show-through artifacts, not text from the neighbouring column - p16.png was checked in full and confirms c1 holds 71-73 and c2 holds 74-76 with no gutter spanning on that page. Faint Hindi show-through from the facing bilingual page is visible on several crops but never overlaps the English text. Two option blocks are printed two-across rather than one-per-line (Q68, Q69 on p15-c2; Q75, Q76 on p16-c2; Q79/Q80 are one-per-line); in each case labels were read left-to-right then down, so printed order (a)(b)(c)(d) is preserved as A/B/C/D. Q79 and Q80 are genuine two-column match grids and are transcribed as GFM pipe tables with the mandatory separator row; the printed colon between the two halves is the column separator and is represented by the pipe, not duplicated as text. Typography normalised to ASCII: curly quotes/apostrophes rendered as straight ones and the en dash in year ranges (2022-23, 2025-26 in Q66) rendered as a hyphen. Wording, numbers and option order are otherwise verbatim. One genuine ambiguity flagged on the item itself: Q70 statement III prints 'up-' at the end of a line and 'skilling' at the start of the next, so the hyphen may be a line-break hyphenation of 'upskilling' rather than a real hyphen; it is transcribed as 'up-skilling' because the surrounding phrase reads 'fresh skilling, and up-skilling'. Q70 statement II likewise breaks 'mainte-/nance' across lines and is joined as 'maintenance' (unambiguous). No defective or duplicate options were found anywhere in the band. No answers are supplied.
